chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect visiting the shrines, all of them: Masjid Quba, for it is the mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day, and the drinking place of Umm Ibrahim, and Masjid Al-Fazeekh, and the graves of the martyrs, and Masjid Al-Ahzaab, and it is Masjid Al-Fath.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it has reached us that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he visited the graves of the martyrs, would say: 'Peace be upon you for what you endured patiently; so good is the final outcome of the Home (Hereafter).'

And let what you say at Masjid Al-Fath be: 'O Helper of the distressed, and O Responder to the supplication of the desperate! Remove my worry, my grief, and my distress, just as You removed from Your Prophet his worry, his grief, and his distress, and sufficed him against the terror of his enemy in this place.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ قُبَاءَ: Masjid Quba, a prominent mosque in Medina
key_terms.مُجِيبَ دَعْوَةِ الْمُضْطَرِّينَ: Responder to the supplication of the desperate

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for visiting shrines and Masjid Al-Fath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the Shia practice of Ziyarah by linking specific sacred sites—such as Masjid Quba, the grave of Imam Ibrahim, and Masjid Al-Fath—to spiritual merit and divine response. It prescribes distinct supplications for martyrs' graves, emphasizing patience as the reward, and for Masjid Al-Fath, invoking Allah to remove distress by mirroring the relief granted to the Prophet, thereby reinforcing the concept of intercession and shared spiritual experience between the Imams and the faithful.
